Chlorine radical.

questions.solution:

$$2(1.0)+5(0.055)=2.275\,\text{t}.$$

**Answer.** $2.275\,\text{t CFC-11-eq}$

**Answer.** 80 μg/L

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: The trophic state index (TSI) = 9.81 × ln(chl-a) + 30.6. If chlorophyll-a = 30 μg/L, the TSI is approximately _____ .

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: A wastewater discharge adds 200 kg/yr of N and 30 kg/yr of P. Using Redfield ratio (C:N:P = 106:16:1, molar masses 12,14,31), the theoretical algal biomass produced is approximately _____ kg (N is limiting).
questions.solution:
**Concept.** N-limited: moles N = 200/14 = 14.29 kmol. P needed = 14.29/16 = 0.893 kmol.

**Working.** C = 106 × 0.893 = 94.6 kmol. Biomass = 94.6 × 12 = 1135 kg.

**Answer.** 1135 kg

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: An algal bloom in a 5 km² lake produces 200 t of biomass with 1% phosphorus content. The phosphorus demand is _____ kg.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** P demand = biomass × P fraction.

**Working.** 200 t × 0.01 = 2 t = 2000 kg.

**Answer.** 2000 kg

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: The nutrient most commonly limiting and therefore triggering eutrophication in freshwater lakes is
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Phosphorus is the most commonly limiting nutrient in freshwater eutrophication.

**Working.** Marine systems are N-limited; freshwater is P-limited.

**Answer.** phosphorus

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: Pre-industrial stratospheric ozone was ~300 DU. The 2023 value over Antarctica is ~280 DU. The percentage depletion is approximately _____ %.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** % depletion = (baseline − current)/baseline × 100.

**Working.** $(300-280)/300 \times 100 = 6.67\%$.

**Answer.** 6.67%

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: UV-B radiation increases by ~2% for each 1% decrease in stratospheric ozone. If ozone drops by 10%, UV-B increases by _____ %.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** UV-B increase ≈ 2% per 1% ozone loss.

**Working.** $10 \times 2\% = 20\%$.

**Answer.** 20%

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: A single Cl atom destroys up to 100,000 O₃ molecules. If 1 kt of CFC-11 (MW=137.4, 3 Cl atoms) is released, theoretical O₃ molecules destroyed ≈ _____ × 10²⁸.

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: The Antarctic ozone hole area is ~25 million km² and the Southern Hemisphere area is 51 million km². The hole covers approximately _____ % of the hemisphere.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** % = hole area / hemisphere area × 100.

**Working.** $25/51 \times 100 = 49.0\%$.

**Answer.** 49.0%

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: The ozone layer is thinnest at approximately _____ km altitude over Antarctica during the ozone hole season.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** The ozone hole centres in the lower stratosphere (~15–20 km).

**Working.** ~18 km.

**Answer.** 18 km

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: The direct radiative forcing of CO₂ is $5.35 \ln(C/C_0)$ W/m². If CO₂ doubles from 280 to 560 ppm, the forcing is _____ W/m².
questions.solution:
**Concept.** $\Delta F = 5.35 \times \ln(560/280) = 5.35 \times \ln(2) = 3.71$.

**Answer.** 3.71 W/m²

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: Methane's direct radiative forcing is $0.036\sqrt{M}$ W/m² (M in ppb). If CH₄ = 1900 ppb, the forcing is approximately _____ W/m².
questions.solution:
**Concept.** $\Delta F = 0.036 \times \sqrt{1900} = 0.036 \times 43.59 = 1.57$.

**Answer.** 1.57 W/m²

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: Anthropogenic CO₂ forcing since pre-industrial (280→420 ppm) is approximately _____ W/m² (use $\Delta F = 5.35 \ln(C/C_0)$).

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: If ECS = 3.0 °C per doubling and CO₂ forcing = 2.17 W/m², the equilibrium warming from CO₂ alone is approximately _____ °C.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** $\Delta T = ECS \times (\Delta F / 3.7) = 3.0 \times (2.17/3.7) = 1.76$.

**Answer.** 1.76 °C

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: Total anthropogenic effective radiative forcing (all agents) as of 2019 is approximately _____ W/m² (IPCC AR6 best estimate).
questions.solution:
**Concept.** IPCC AR6 Table 7.8: total ERF ≈ 2.72 W/m².

**Answer.** 2.72 W/m²

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: Water vapour accounts for approximately _____ % of the natural greenhouse effect by contribution.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Water vapour contributes ~60%.

**Answer.** 60%

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: A livestock operation emits 80 t CH₄ and 1200 t CO₂. Total GWP-weighted emission (CH₄ GWP₁₀₀ = 28) is _____ t CO₂-e.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Total = CO₂ + CH₄ × GWP.

**Working.** $1200 + 80 \times 28 = 3440$.

**Answer.** 3440 t CO₂-e

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: A country's inventory: 500 Mt CO₂ (energy), 100 Mt CO₂-e (agriculture CH₄), 50 Mt CO₂-e (industry N₂O). Energy sector share is _____ %.

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: A cement plant emits 200 t CO₂ from fuel and 150 t CO₂ from calcination. Total process + energy CO₂ = _____ t.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Total = fuel + process.

**Working.** $200 + 150 = 350$.

**Answer.** 350 t CO₂

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: Which of the following has the highest global warming potential (GWP₁₀₀) per unit mass?
questions.solution:
**Concept.** SF6 has the highest GWP100 (23500) of all greenhouse gases.

**Working.** SF6 GWP >> N2O (265) >> CH4 (28) >> CO2 (1).

**Answer.** SF6

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: At ~40 Gt CO₂/yr global emissions, the remaining budget for 1.5 °C (~500 Gt CO₂) is exhausted in _____ years.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Years = budget / rate.

**Working.** $500 / 40 = 12.5$.

**Answer.** 12.5 years

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: Global CO₂ emissions in 2023 were ~36.8 Gt. A country emitting 5 Gt has a _____ % share.

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: If the remaining budget for 2 °C is 1150 Gt CO₂ and annual emissions are 40 Gt, the budget is exhausted in approximately _____ years.

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: A country's cumulative emissions are 150 Gt CO₂ and its fair-share budget is 200 Gt. At 2 Gt/yr, years to exhaust remaining budget is _____ years.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Remaining = 200 − 150 = 50 Gt. Years = 50/2 = 25.

**Answer.** 25 years

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: If remaining budget = 400 Gt, current emissions = 40 Gt/yr, declining linearly to 20 Gt/yr over 20 years, average emissions are _____ Gt/yr.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Average = (initial + final)/2 for linear decline.

**Working.** $(40+20)/2 = 30$.

**Answer.** 30 Gt/yr

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: Methyl bromide has ODP = 0.66. If 100 t is released, the CFC-11-equivalent is _____ t.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** $100 \times 0.66 = 66$.

**Answer.** 66 t CFC-11-eq

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: CFC-12 (ODP=0.82) and HCFC-22 (ODP=0.055). 3 t CFC-12 + 10 t HCFC-22. Total ODP-weighted emission = _____ t CFC-11-eq.

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: 500 kg CFC-113 (ODP=0.85) + 200 kg CCl₄ (ODP=1.1). Total CFC-11-equivalent = _____ kg.

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: HCFC-22 has ODP = 0.055. If 200 t is released, the CFC-11-equivalent is _____ t.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** $200 \times 0.055 = 11$.

**Answer.** 11 t CFC-11-eq

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: How many Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) were adopted by the UN in 2015?
questions.solution:
**Concept.** The 2030 Agenda includes 17 SDGs.

**Answer.** 17

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: The target year for achieving all 17 SDGs is
questions.solution:
**Concept.** 2030 Agenda sets 2030 as deadline.

**Answer.** 2030

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: SDG 15 targets to conserve at least _____ % of terrestrial and inland freshwater ecosystems by 2020.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Target 15.5: at least 10%.

**Answer.** 10%

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: SDG 7 targets a _____ % share of renewable energy in total global energy by 2030.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** IEA estimates ~36% RE share by 2030 for SDG 7.

**Answer.** 36%

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: If a country's renewable energy share is 25% and it aims for 75% by 2030, the required increase is _____ percentage points.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** $75 - 25 = 50$.

**Answer.** 50 percentage points

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: Which of the following SDGs have direct environmental targets?
questions.solution:
**Concept.** All four SDGs have direct environmental targets.

**Working.** SDG 6 (water), 7 (clean energy), 11 (sustainable cities), 14 (life below water) all have explicit environmental targets.

**Answer.** All four SDGs

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: Mercury can travel _____ distances in the atmosphere due to its long residence time (~0.5–2 years).
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Long atmospheric residence enables hemispheric transport.

**Answer.** Thousands of km

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: The LRTAP Convention was adopted in _____ year — the first international treaty on air pollution.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Convention on Long-Range Transboundary Air Pollution, 1979.

**Answer.** 1979

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: Country A emits 500 kt SO₂. 30% deposited in Country B. Country B's own emissions = 400 kt. Total deposition in Country B = _____ kt.

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: A factory emits 100 t lead annually. 25% deposited locally. Local deposition = _____ t.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** $100 \times 0.25 = 25$.

**Answer.** 25 t

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: Transboundary air pollution was first addressed internationally by the
questions.solution:
**Concept.** The Convention on Long-Range Transboundary Air Pollution (LRTAP, 1979) was the first international treaty on air pollution.

**Working.** LRTAP predates Stockholm and Rotterdam.

**Answer.** LRTAP Convention (1979)

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: Sea level has risen approximately _____ mm over the 20th century (1900–2000).
questions.solution:
**Concept.** ~170 mm global mean sea level rise in the 20th century.

**Answer.** 170 mm

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: Global mean temperature has risen by approximately _____ °C since the pre-industrial era (as of 2023).
questions.solution:
**Concept.** IPCC AR6: ~1.2 °C above 1850–1900 levels.

**Answer.** 1.2 °C

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: A glacier retreats at 30 m/yr horizontally. Surface slopes at 15°. Vertical thinning rate = _____ m/yr.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Vertical = horizontal × tan(slope).

**Working.** $30 \times \tan(15°) = 8.04$.

**Answer.** 8.04 m/yr

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: Sea level rises 0.5 m. 60% of a 100 km² low-lying island is below 0.5 m. Area lost = _____ km².
questions.solution:
**Concept.** $100 \times 0.60 = 60$.

**Answer.** 60 km²

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: Coral bleaching kills 40% of corals on a 500 ha reef. Intact reef supports 500 kg fish/ha. Lost fishery productivity = _____ kg.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Lost = area × productivity.

**Working.** $500 \times 0.40 \times 500 = 100{,}000$.

**Answer.** 100,000 kg

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: India's installed renewable energy capacity exceeded _____ GW by end of 2023.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** ~180 GW installed RE by end of 2023.

**Answer.** 180 GW

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: India's per-capita CO₂ is ~2.0 t/yr vs US ~14.0 t/yr. India's per-capita is approximately _____ % of US level.

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: India's coal production ~800 Mt. Carbon content 60%, 3.67 t CO₂/t C. CO₂ from coal ≈ _____ Mt.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** $800 \times 0.60 \times 3.67 = 1761.6$.

**Answer.** 1762 Mt CO₂

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: NCAP aims for a _____ % reduction in PM2.5 and PM10 by 2026 in 131 non-attainment cities.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** NCAP target: 40% reduction.

**Answer.** 40%

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: India's coal power capacity ~210 GW at 60% PLF. Annual coal consumption for power ≈ _____ Mt (0.8 t coal/MWh).

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: Environmental justice originated in the US in 1982 from protests against a landfill in which county?
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Warren County, NC (1982).

**Answer.** Warren County, North Carolina

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: A community's cancer risk is 50 per million from industrial pollution. EPA threshold is 100 per million. Risk is _____ % of threshold.

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: Low-income area 2 km from a polluter, high-income 20 km. Concentration decays as 1/r². Ratio (low:high) ≈ _____ .

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: Environmental justice primarily addresses the disproportionate exposure of marginalized communities to
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Environmental justice addresses disproportionate exposure to environmental hazards in marginalized communities.

**Working.** The core concern is unequal pollution burden.

**Answer.** Environmental hazards and pollution

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: The Stockholm Declaration (1972) established how many principles on the human environment?
questions.solution:
**Concept.** 26 principles.

**Answer.** 26

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: The Rio Declaration (1992) established how many principles for sustainable development?
questions.solution:
**Concept.** 27 principles.

**Answer.** 27

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: Under the Basel Convention, hazardous waste exports require _____ informed consent from the importing country.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Prior Informed Consent (PIC).

**Answer.** Prior informed

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: A shipping company violates MARPOL and discharges 500 t oily waste. Maximum penalty under international law ≈ _____ million USD.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** MARPOL violations carry severe penalties.

**Answer.** 10 million USD

questions.subject: Global & Regional Issues
questions.stem: The Ramsar Convention has designated approximately _____ million hectares of wetlands as Ramsar Sites globally.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** ~2,500 sites covering ~250 million ha.

**Answer.** 250 million hectares
